neighbours.label: opening or unlocking a door or gate (peaks on 'open(ing)', 'unlock', or the word before 'door'/'gate')
fire: A service dog can help its owner by opening doors around the house.
Swipe the badge on the reader to open the main gate.
The janitor came early every morning to unlock the doors of the school.
A new automatic electric gate now guards the driveway.
She fumbled with her keys and finally managed to open the front door.
Pull the green lever to open the barn door from inside.
The guard pressed a switch and began opening the gate for the lorry.
Use the brass key to unlock the door at the end of the corridor.
quiet: A service dog can help its owner by fetching slippers around the house.
Swipe the badge on the reader to record your working hours.
The janitor came early every morning to sweep the floors of the school.
A new automatic electric lamp now lights the driveway.
She fumbled with her keys and finally dropped them in the mud.
Pull the green lever to lower the hay from the loft.
The guard pressed a switch and began weighing the lorry.
Use the brass bell to call the porter at the end of the corridor.

notes: Top examples: 'opening doors', 'open a door', 'electric gate'; output direction suppresses ' door', ' gate'. Probes: 'opening doors' 0.70, 'electric gate' 0.70, 'unlock the door' 0.51, 'open the garage gate' 0.38; 'opened a bank account' 0.12, 'start the washing machine' 0.18.
